Camping 101: First Aid directs adventurers with medical training to seek out Nurse Neela in Brill. By learning to construct a First Aid Kit for their campsites, travelers can provide life-saving treatment and recuperation while surviving deep in the wilderness.

Venturing beyond fortified settlements carries constant physical danger, from hostile beasts to opposing factions. For traveling practitioners of First Aid, learning to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit allows an ordinary wilderness resting stop to serve as a mobile field clinic, patching up wounds and restoring vitality far from civil infrastructure.

In the Forsaken town of Brill, Nurse Neela provides instruction on turning basic medical expertise into practical camp equipment. Once a traveler demonstrates sufficient skill in bandaging and treatment, she shares the techniques required to construct a portable kit. Setting up such equipment requires a proper wilderness site centered around a basic campfire, which standard cooking instructors can teach travelers to build.

Nurse Neela is a medical practitioner located in the Forsaken settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. She instructs skilled First Aid practitioners on how to craft First Aid Kits designed for field campsites.

Camping 101: First Aid directs travelers to Shen'dar Village to learn how to fashion essential medical supplies for a wilderness camp. By seeking out Naleeia Tattermend, skilled practitioners can create camp kits capable of treating injuries and saving lives far from civilization.

Life on the road across Azeroth is fraught with violence, wild beasts, and environmental hazards. For any traveler, learning First Aid is as practical as it is honorable, ensuring that bloodied cuts and broken bones can be bound without relying purely on spellcraft. Establishing a dedicated First Aid Kit at a wilderness camp provides a reliable center for healing, allowing exhausted adventurers to recover and tend to their companions before moving on.

Not every field medic knows how to properly assemble durable camp medical supplies. In Shen'dar Village, a specialist named Naleeia Tattermend instructs dedicated practitioners in the art of fashioning campsite First Aid Kits. Those seeking her guidance must first demonstrate their own proficiency in basic medical care before she reveals her techniques.

Camping 101: Fishing directs aspiring anglers to discover how their patience with a rod and line can elevate wilderness expeditions. By seeking out Fenn Fairweather in Shen'dar Village, proficient fishermen can learn to craft a decorative Fish Bowl fixture to bolster morale and camp comfort.

Life in the wilderness demands more than sharp blades and sturdy armor; keeping morale high in the field can mean the difference between triumph and exhaustion. While fishing is often treated purely as a quiet pastime or a means to harvest provisions, skilled anglers can turn their craft toward improving campsite comfort. By capturing live fish and preparing dedicated fixtures, a traveler can transform a bleak encampment into a welcoming sanctuary.

In Shen'dar Village, the artisan Fenn Fairweather shares trade secrets with seasoned fishermen who understand the patience of the rod and reel. Those who demonstrate sufficient skill can learn to fashion a Fish Bowl—a simple camp fixture designed to bring cheer and relaxation to weary companions. Maintaining high spirits out in the wilds helps keep party members focused and resolute when facing looming dangers.

Camping 101: Leatherworking directs fledgling leatherworkers to seek advanced instruction on crafting durable wilderness shelters. Guided to Indari Sunseam in Shen'dar Village, craftsmen learn to stitch protective tents that offer essential rest across long expeditions into the wilds.

Such shelters keep adventurers dry during relentless downpours and cool beneath blazing suns, ensuring they stay well-rested throughout long journeys.

Pitching a tent requires respect for civil boundaries, as townsfolk take issue with crude campsites cluttering municipal streets. Camps must be pitched out in the wild. Furthermore, a sturdy shelter is only half the equation: no campsite is complete without a warming campfire, prompting adventurers to visit a local cook to pick up basic firemaking skills before striking out into the wilds.

Nature's Call is a Shadowglen quest where the dryad Tarindrella seeks to uncover why the local Gnarlpine furbolgs suddenly turned against their long-standing night elf allies. By gathering carved totems from their abandoned camps, adventurers help reveal the distressing spiritual corruption spreading through Teldrassil.

Nature's Call is an investigative mission in Shadowglen given by the dryad Tarindrella. Refusing to believe that the Gnarlpine furbolg would abandon centuries of friendship with the night elves without reason, she asks travelers to comb through the furbolgs' hastily abandoned camps along the western border of the glen to recover intact engraved totems.

Deciphering the recovered totems reveals a tragic descent into madness. The Gnarlpine were plagued by recurring nightmares of an encroaching shadow destined to wipe them out. Over time, sheer terror curdled into blind rage, warping their minds until they viewed their longtime elven neighbors as the very shadow they feared. Tarindrella hopes these findings will shed light on the deeper malaise creeping through Teldrassil.

The Trial of Cunning and Stealth

To draw upon the power of the great cat spirit, aspirants must prove they possess the temperament of the predator. True harmony with the cat demands an understanding of cunning and patience, paired with explosive ferocity when cornered. The spirit does not grant its gift lightly to those who simply demand power; instead, it tests whether a seeker can think, move, and strike like the feline hunters of the wild. Only by demonstrating these inner traits can an initiate hope to earn the right to take the cat's physical shape.

The test sends seekers into the gloom of the nearby Stormrage Barrow Den, located just east of the spirit's avatar. Deep within these subterranean halls lie three sacred tokens: the Relic of the Fang, the Relic of the Claw, and the Relic of the Silent Shadow. However, claiming them is far from straightforward. The barrow den has become infested with enraged spirits that violently strike at any intruder on sight. To survive the cavern and reach the relics, a seeker cannot rely on brute force alone, but must tread carefully through the darkness.

At the center of this trial is the Avatar of Saeyleenan, the physical manifestation through which the Great Windborne Cat Spirit speaks to young initiates. Understanding that untutored seekers lack the natural stealth of a seasoned predator, a statue placed at the entrance of the barrow den offers a temporary blessing of concealment. Those who successfully slip past the frenzied spirits and return all three relics prove they have absorbed the lessons of the predator. In return, the Avatar recognizes their worthiness and imparts the blessing needed to assume the cat form.

Kaltunk evaluates every eager recruit, tempering dreams of wrestling demons and dragons with the practical duties ahead. Training begins in the canyon, where recruits learn humility before claiming glory.

Gornek waits beside the camp fire, only steps away from Kaltunk. The gruff veteran regards fresh arrivals with a skeptical eye and often grumbles about the meager stock reaching camp. His duty is to harden these young fighters through trials, starting with the vermin that threaten the encampment's supplies.
